title: Technology Sector Update for 05/08/2018: ZBRA,VECO,XCRA,COHU,JD

Technology stocks were drifting higher in late Tuesday trade, with shares of tech companies in the S&P 500 adding almost 0.2% in value today while the Philadelphia semiconductor index was posting a nearly 0.6% advance.
Among technology stocks moving on news:
+ Zebra Technologies ( ZBRA ) jumped over 14% on Tuesday to reach a new, all-time high of $157.18 a share, after the automatic identification and data capture company recorded non-GAAP Q1 net income and revenue exceeding Wall Street estimates. Excluding one-time items, it earned $2.56 per share during the three months ended March 31, up from $1.37 per share during the year-ago period and topping the Capital IQ consensus by $0.51 per share. Total revenue increased to $977 million from $865 million during the same period last year ago and also beating $935.9 million consensus calla. Zebra also raised its FY18 sales projectons to a new range of 6% to 9% over its $3.72 billion in FY17 sales, or between $3.94 million to $4.05 billion, compared with its prior outlook expecting 4% to 7% growth and matching the analyst consensus expecting $3.94 billion in revenue.
In other sector news:
+ Excerra Corp ( XCRA ) raced to an 11-year high on Tuesday, topping out at its best share price since July 2007 at $13.62 apiece after agreeing to a $796 million buyout from Cohu Inc ( COHU ). Under terms of the stock-and-cash deal, Excerra investors will receive $9.00 in cash and 0.2109 of a Cohu common share for each share they now own, valuing the target company at $13.92 a share. Cohu said it expects the transaction will immediately add to its adjusted per-share earnings after closing, expected during the second half of 2018.
+ Veeco Instruments ( VECO ) jumped out to more than a 14% advance on Tuesday after the electronic components company beat analyst estimates with its Q1 net income and revenue. Excluding one-time items, it earned $0.20 per share during the January-to-March fiscal period, almost doubling its $0.11 per share non-GAAP profit last year and easily beating the Capital IQ consensus by $0.14 per share. Revenue increased to $158.6 million from $94.5 million last year and also exceeding the $151.62 million Street view. For the current quarter, Veeco is expecting non-GAAP earnings in a range of $0.01 to $0.20 per share on between $145 million to $170 million in revenue. Analysts are expecting adjusted Q2 net income of $0.13 per share on $158 million in revenue.
- JD.com ( JD ) dropped almost 5% on Tuesday after the Chinese e-commerce company reported Q1 net income trailing Wall Street expectations despite a larger-than-expected 33% increase in revenue for the January-to-March quarter. Excluding one-time items, the company earned RMB0.71 per American depository share compared with RMB0.92 per ADS during the same quarter last year and lagging the Capital IQ consensus by RMB0.11 per ADS. It also generated RMB100.1 billion in revenue during the quarter, topping the $98.92 billion analyst mean.
